points.en: white stripe on the wing coverts (male)

art.subject: Pied Bush Chat (Saxicola caprata), adult male in spring: head, back, wings, breast and belly black with a faint gloss; a long white stripe on the inner wing coverts of the folded wing; rump and uppertail coverts pure white; vent and undertail coverts white; tail entirely black; bill black; eye dark; legs black.
art.pose: perched upright on the top of a low bush, side view, wings slightly drooped and tail flicked
art.scene: open grassy farmland edge with low shrubs on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in May, clear daylight; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched upright on a bush top with the wings slightly drooped: glossy black head, back, breast and wings, long white stripe on the inner wing coverts, white rump and uppertail coverts, white lower belly and vent, all-black tail, short thin black bill, black legs

adult female, side view perched upright: dull dark brown upperparts, rufous-brown underparts with faint darker streaks, rufous rump and uppertail coverts, dark brown wings without white, dark brown tail, thin dark bill
art.build: A small, compact chat about the size of a sparrow, similar in size and shape to Stejneger's Stonechat: round head, short neck and an upright stance. Bill short, thin, straight and black, much shorter than the head. Legs slender, black, of medium length. Wings fairly short; at rest the wingtips reach only a short way down the tail. Tail short-medium and square-ended, often flicked together with the wings. Perches conspicuously upright on bush tops, tall weeds and fence posts, dropping to the ground for insects; in flight the white rump and white wing stripe flash against the otherwise black plumage.
avoid: Do not give the male an orange breast, a white neck patch or white underparts; those belong to Stejneger's Stonechat (Saxicola stejnegeri).
Do not paint white in the tail; the tail is all black, and the white is only on the rump, the wing stripe and the vent.
Do not add a white supercilium, white throat or white crown.
Do not paint brown scaling on the male's black plumage; spring males are clean black.
